newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as wheat declines.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as wheat declines.

text.p: A drop in nearby wheat contracts pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
Trading was quiet and volume was thin before the U.S. Thanksgiving Day Holiday. Markets closed early Wednesday at 1210 CST and also will close early Friday at 1210 CST.

Position squaring was noted before the release Friday of USDA's weekly export sales report. Friday also is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT December contracts and the market is expecting light deliveries of corn, under one million bushels, to be posted for delivery.

The session high of $2.74 was set near the open and technicians cited first resistance in the December at $2.74-1/4 and second resistance at $2.76-1/2. First support was at $2.72 and second support was at $2.70.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, below the 81,826 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Corn options volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, below the 13,010 traded Tuesday.
Corn futures closed two cents per bushel lower to 1/4 higher, with December down 1-1/4 at $2.72.
